There is something really concerning (and disappointing) going on in the US right now.
A dangerous and preventable situation.
Let me explain.
1/

In early 2022 a new variant of H5N1 bird flu made its way to the US.
It wasn’t subtle.  It quickly swept the country and caused massive bird mortality among all different bird types.
2/

Remember a few years ago when eggs were more expensive than beef?  H5N1 was the reason.  It is extremely pathogenic to chickens.
3/

There were a number of spillovers from H5N1 into various mammals, but most of these were fairly contained.
4/

Then something completely unexpected happened.  In late 2023 or early 2024, H5N1 started showing up in the mammary tissue of dairy cattle.  It was a major outbreak.
5/

It took several months to figure out this was happening, and by then the virus had spread to herds across the country.
6/

Pasteurization kills H5N1, so there haven’t been any human cases from drinking pasteurized milk.  However, it caused a lot of damage and maintained an enormous outbreak in mammals (not where we want it circulating).
7/

The USDA tried to contain the outbreak by preventing the transport of lactating cattle across state lines unless they test negative for H5N1.  It wasn’t enough though.
8/

This should have ended 2 years ago.  It is SUPER easy to screen herds for the virus (bulk milk testing).
Infected cattle clear the virus after a few weeks.  The outbreak could have been stopped (and still can be) if we had the will to enforce strict quarantines.

We don’t.
9/

Here’s the other disappointing part.  This is a phylogenetic tree of the H5N1 lineages since the start.  Notice how all of the sequences from this year cluster together?
10/

If you look at where those sequences came from you see that they are from all over the country.  That means the virus is not contained, it’s continuing to move across the country.
11/

The fear is that with time the virus will adapt to mammalian transmission and start infecting other mammalian species, which is happening already (and we aren’t doing much about it).
12/

Among those species is human.
So far there hasn’t been sustained human-to-human transmission, but if we keep giving the virus  chances, it is just a matter of time.
13/13

hits.draft_en:
The US H5N1 situation in dairy herds is a slow-motion failure, and it was avoidable.

Short version:
- A new bird flu variant landed in early 2022 and killed huge numbers of birds. It's the reason eggs once cost more than beef.
- In late 2023 or early 2024 it jumped into the mammary tissue of dairy cattle. Months passed before anyone caught it, and by then herds nationwide were infected.
- Pasteurized milk has caused no human cases. The danger is a massive outbreak circulating in mammals.

The fix is not complicated. Bulk milk testing screens herds cheaply, infected animals clear the virus within weeks, and strict quarantines would end it. Moving only test-negative lactating cows across state lines did not go far enough.

This year's sequences cluster together and come from all over the country, so the virus is still on the move. Each new mammal infection is another shot at adapting, humans included. No sustained person-to-person spread so far.

running AI on your own hardware

It helps you turn natural-language requests into Studio changes by connecting agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini to scripts, instances, terrain, lighting, and assets.

Key features:

• Direct Studio control – agents can create and modify scripts, instances, properties, terrain, lighting, and assets
• Multi-Place routing – connect up to five Studio windows and target work by Studio ID
• Bidirectional sync – review local and Studio changes before applying them
• Automated Playtest – run structured Play sessions that inspect UI, deliver input, and record evidence
• Asset workflow – save images locally, upload them through Roblox Open Cloud, and apply returned URIs in Studio

It’s open-source (AGPL-3.0 license).

▲ Nace AI just released Drex for Search, which brings its Drex decision models to document search, so AI agents get cited pages instead of top-k chunks.

The key idea is that search is a series of decisions. Drex first classifies the question as a quick lookup or a deeper agent search. It then narrows the workspace from folder to file, section and page, down to table and column inside a sheet. Only the kept pages reach the LLM, and the answer cites the file and page.

The numbers, per Nace: 92.05% on BrowseComp-Plus with GPT-5, at 12.61 search calls per question, 16.6x fewer than the only entry ahead. 77.5% R@1 on VisDocAgentBench, 10 points above Claude Opus 5. 94.7% on MADQA with Gemini 3.5 Flash. On OfficeQA Pro, all 9 agent setups Nace tested needed fewer turns, with Claude Code on Opus 5.5 going from 18.5 to 9.1 turns.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode can call it through the nace-mcp server or the CLI. There are also Python and TypeScript SDKs and a REST API......

virals.name: Shlomo F.
virals.text:
My bio literally says I'm a "professional" vibe coder. So when a new study measured what vibe coding actually costs, I had to read it. Mostly out of self-defense.

Researchers collected almost 18,000 real coding agent sessions from public GitHub repos. Mostly Claude Code, but also Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others. Real devs, real projects, not a benchmark.

They split them into three types. The human writes everything. The human and the agent write it together. Or vibe coding, where the agent writes over 99% of the code.

Vibe coding went from under 20% of sessions in February to over 50% recently. So at least I'm not alone.

Now the bad part. Per 100 lines that actually made it into a commit, vibe coding was:
The most expensive: $2.71, vs $0.92 when working together
The slowest: 10.7 minutes, vs 5.5 together
The least secure: almost 4x the vulnerabilities of human-written code

And here's what actually surprised me. Working together wasn't just better than vibe coding. It was also cheaper and faster than writing everything by hand.

So the fastest way to code right now isn't the AI doing everything, and it isn't you doing everything. It's the annoying middle, where you actually read what it wrote.

The other number explains why. Users pushed back on the agent in about half of their prompts, even in vibe coding sessions. "That's wrong." "No, the other file." Meanwhile the agent asked a clarifying question in about 3% of its turns.

So half the conversation is you correcting it, and it almost never asks before guessing. So half the conversation is you correcting it, and it almost never asks before guessing.

Turns out vibe coding is just code review where you skip the reading and pay extra.

To be fair, these are early adopters who chose to log their sessions, so it's not everyone. But it's one of the first looks at how people actually use these agents, not how they score on a benchmark.

I'm keeping the "professional" in my bio though. I'm just going to start earning it.

So be honest. Vibe, together, or still typing it all yourself?

اعتقد ٩٩ ريال ، مو متذكر .

سعره غالي ؟ نعم بالتأكيد 

عضوي 🌱 
صيد حر 
كمية بروتين ٣٤ جم 
زيت الزيتون البكر الممتاز العضوي 🌱 
غني بالاوميجا ثري ٢٢٠٠ مج 

انا ادفع زيادة مقابل جودة المنتج . لاني اهتم بغذائي و غذاء من حولي بشكل كبير . و السوق فيه منتجات عديدة تتفاوت في جودتها و اسعارها ، بس الاكيد :

جميعها مطابق للمواصفات و المقاييس السعودية ✅ 
جميعها آمنة للاستهلاك باذن الله ✅ 
طبعاً ، مو كل شيء آمن للاستهلاك معناته ذات قيمة غذائية و صحية ، و لكن كل شيء صحي فهو اكيد باذن الله آمن للاستهلاك .

و اخيراً ، صحي لا يعني انه ينفع للجميع باختلاف اوضاعهم الصحية ، السكر العضوي و الكربوهيدرات العضوية قد لا تكون افضل خيار لمرضى السكري على سبيل المثال اذا تم استهلاكها بكميات كبيرة .

ما شاء الله تبارك الله ، الله يوسع عليك و يزيد رزقك و الجميع يا رب .

يا جماعة يشتري زيتون بالحبة ، و الا يزرع البذر عشان ما عاد يشتري زيتون و يوفر فلوس ، و الا يشتري شبيه الزيتون … حياته و عايشها زي ما يبي . هو مبسوط ما شاء الله و عائلته مبسوطة مع انه ما طلب رأينا و رأينا غير مهم اطلاقاً في امور مثل هذي .

عجبك المحتوى اللي يقدمه اهلاً و سهلاً ، ما عجبك فقط تجاهله . مع اني بصريح العبارة لا اتفق مع بعض محتواه الا اني مستحيل اطلق عليه صفة البخيل . قضية انه نكون اوصياء الله على خلقه و ننقد الشخص في امور شخصية بحتة مثل الادارة المالية ما لها سنع ، هو ما قال لك لازم تسوي مثلي . 

الدكتور أيمن يمشي بمبدأ " اذا ما عاملت الريال كأنه مليون ريال ما راح توصل لمرحلة تصرف المليون ريال و كأنه ريال " 👏🏻

تعلموا الاختلاف ، و احترام الاختلاف . 

عاد الدكتور أيمن لو يطّلع على ادارتي المالية يمكن يسوي لي جلسة مناصحة 😪😂

✨

posts.text:
THIS IS INSANE. MY KID’S PLUSH OWL HAD A CAMERA BEHIND ONE EYE

I spent a week using Grok Bot to analyze what was on the circuit board I found inside. On the seventh night, I opened a video file showing the room where we kept the toy.

It started with a reflection.

From across the room, both eyes looked pitch black. Up close, I noticed a tiny circle behind the plastic of one eye. I shone my phone’s flashlight on it—the circle remained.

I pulled out the batteries and tore open the seam.

Tucked behind the stuffing was a small circuit board, with wires running toward the face and a lens positioned exactly where that circle had been.

I’m a developer, so I told myself I’d spend just an hour figuring it out.

Seven evenings later, the owl was still lying in pieces next to my keyboard.

My first attempt to probe the device failed. I checked the connections, saved a memory dump, read it again, and compared the two copies.

Then, I began sifting through the files using Grok Bot.

→ 12 video clips
→ 7 audio files
→ 23 logged events

I kept searching for an explanation—something that would make me feel foolish for having been worried in the first place.

Then, I opened the camera settings:

trigger=low_light

The event log showed this:

03:14:07 → low light detected
03:14:07 → recording started
03:14:12 → recording stopped

I opened the corresponding five-second clip. I recognized the curtains before I recognized the angle.

The camera was looking out from the shelf where we’d put the owl.

The video compresses that entire week into 35 seconds. Breakdown below ↓

posts.text:
Elon said to treat Grok Bot like a super competent hire. So I gave it the night shift and one rule.

That was the one rule I gave it before bed: do the work, send nothing without my yes.

Grok Bot has an official Chief of Staff job on its use cases page. It reads your Slack, email, calendar and meeting notes and tells you what's new and what to do about it.

Elon said to use it like you're hiring a super competent employee. So I hired it for the night shift.

What was waiting at 7am:

- 63 email drafts, sorted by who's waiting longest
- 3 threads flagged urgent, each with why it matters
- 2 meetings it wanted me to drop, with the reason
- 1 invoice reply ready, amount left blank for me
- 0 messages sent

In 1986 a guy got kicked out of every casino in Vegas for counting cards. So he flew to Hong Kong with $180,000 and started betting on horses instead.

He walked away with almost $900 million.

It was Bill Benter.

He realized horse racing was just another counting problem  same math, more moving parts.

He and a partner built a computer model that estimated the true odds of each horse. If his numbers showed an edge, he bet. If not, he skipped it.

That’s the whole trick:

Expected value.

EV = p · b − (1 − p)

Only bet when the probability of winning × the potential payout is greater than the chance of losing.

What’s even crazier is that Benter once gave a 45-minute lecture explaining the math behind his system.

That recording was never supposed to become public.

And almost nobody knows it exists.

This is the lecture that professional bettors and hedge fund analysts studied.

The answer is in this video.

How to Fine-Tune Your Own AI Model in a Browser, No Code Required (FULL GUIDE)

Most people use open-source models as they are. The ones getting real results train them on their own data

You don't need a research lab for that. One repo gives you a web interface where you pick a model, pick a dataset and press Start

It's called LlamaFactory. 75k+ stars on GitHub, Apache-2.0 license, published at ACL 2024. Amazon, NVIDIA and Aliyun use it

GitHub:

■ What you get

• Models: Llama, Qwen3, DeepSeek, Gemma, GLM, Mistral, Phi, GPT-OSS, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA (100+ in total)
• Training approaches: pre-training, SFT, reward modeling, PPO, DPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO
• Methods: full tuning, freeze, LoRA, QLoRA (2 to 8-bit)
• Speed tricks built in: FlashAttention-2, Unsloth, Liger Kernel
• Tracking: LlamaBoard, TensorBoard, W&B, MLflow, SwanLab
• Deploy: OpenAI-style API with vLLM or SGLang

■ Guide: from zero to your own model

① Install (Python 3.11+)

git clone --depth 1
cd LlamaFactory
pip install -e .
pip install -r requirements/metrics.txt

② Launch the GUI

llamafactory-cli webui

Opens LLaMA Board in your browser. Train, Evaluate, Chat and Export live in one place

③ Prepare your data

Put a JSON file in the data folder. Alpaca format is the simplest:

• instruction - the task (required)
• input - extra context (optional)
• output - the answer you want (required)

Then register the file in data/dataset_info.json. It will show up in the GUI dropdown

④ Configure in the Train tab

• Choose a model (start with a 4B or 8B instruct)
• Choose Supervised Fine-Tuning with LoRA
• Select your dataset
• Hit Preview command to see the exact config
• Press Start and watch the loss curve live

⑤ Test it

Load your LoRA adapter in the Chat tab and talk to the result

Use the SAME template in training and inference, otherwise outputs get weird

⑥ Ship it

Export merges the LoRA into the base model

Or serve it as an API that works with any ChatGPT-compatible app:

API_PORT=8000 llamafactory-cli api examples/inference/qwen3.yaml infer_backend=vllm

Prefer the terminal? The whole pipeline is 3 commands:

• llamafactory-cli train examples/train_lora/qwen3_lora_sft.yaml
• llamafactory-cli chat examples/inference/qwen3_lora_sft.yaml
• llamafactory-cli export examples/merge_lora/qwen3_lora_sft.yaml

■ What to know before you start

• Quality of the dataset decides everything. 500 clean examples beat 50,000 messy ones
• Check the license of the base model you pick. Apache-2.0 on LlamaFactory doesn't cover model weights
• Some models and datasets on Hugging Face are gated. Run huggingface-cli login first

Fine-tuning is no longer about code or budget. It's about data
